findings.summary: AxiosError.from copies only message, code, name and cause instead of all own properties of the source error, so fields like errno, syscall, address, port and hostname are lost.
AxiosError.from throws a TypeError on a null/undefined error, no longer falls back to 'Error' for message or name, and `code || error.code` wrongly overrides an explicit falsy code.

isAxiosError (and __CANCEL__ in CanceledError) became own enumerable properties instead of non-enumerable prototype ones, and cause is now enumerable and assigned unconditionally, so they show up in Object.keys, spreads, toEqual and JSON.stringify and may overwrite an existing cause.
__CANCEL__ is now an own enumerable property rather than non-enumerable on the prototype, changing enumeration, serialization and equality behavior.
this.status = response.status leaves status undefined when the response has no status, where the old code set it to null.
New tests call require('node:util/types') inside an ESM spec, which fails in browser/Karma runs because process.release can exist while require does not.
New tests call require('node:util/types') inside an ESM spec, which fails in browser/Karma runs, and they don't cover from() regressions such as property copying or an empty error.
